_comment: Text prompts for the ElevenLabs sound-generation API, one per cue name in
sfx.json and per bed kind in sources/music.py. These live in style/ rather
than in code because the wording is an editorial choice the author should be
able to tune without touching the generator.
Every prompt ends with negative guidance ('no music', 'no melody'). Without
it the model tends to score the cue -- it adds pads and tonal movement to a
one-second hit, which is exactly wrong for a documentary where the bed and
the SFX layer are mixed separately and ducked independently.
Beds also say 'continuous' and 'unchanging': a bed is tiled to span length
(see soundgen.tile_to_duration), so anything with a beginning or an end
fights the tiling instead of surviving it.

sfx.vhs-burst: short burst of analog VHS tape static, harsh magnetic tape head noise, abrupt, dry, no music
sfx.static-crackle: crackling analog radio static, electrical interference, dry hiss and pops, no music
sfx.sub-drop: deep cinematic sub bass drop, descending low frequency sweep, dark, ominous, no music
sfx.bass-thud: single deep bass drum thud, low muffled impact, tight, no reverb tail, no music
sfx.glitch-sting: short digital glitch sting, data corruption artifact, harsh high frequency chatter, no music
sfx.metal-scrape: harsh metal scrape, rusted steel dragging slowly across concrete, gritty, dry, no music
sfx.heartbeat: slow human heartbeat heard through a chest, deep muffled double thump, no music

beds.drone-low: sustained low dark ambient drone, deep sub bass, minimal, unchanging, continuous texture, no melody, no rhythm, no percussion
beds.drone-tense: tense dark ambient drone, dissonant low strings, faint metallic ringing, unresolved dread, continuous, no melody, no rhythm, no percussion
beds.pulse-slow: slow pulsing dark ambient drone, deep sub bass swelling and receding, minimal, continuous, no melody, no percussion
